newsitem.title: CANADA: Bovar ordered to step up Swan Hills tests.
newsitem.headline: Bovar ordered to step up Swan Hills tests.

text.p: Alberta said on Thursday it ordered Bovar Inc unit Chem-Security to boost environmental monitoring at its Swan Hills hazardous waste treatment plant after finding high toxic chemical levels last year.
The Alberta Environmental Protection ministry said the company would be required to expand current procedures to include vegetation sampling and more animal testing than before.

Tests conducted last year by provincial officials revealed high levels of polychlorinated biphenyls (PCBs), dioxins and furans in wild game meat samples within a 30-km radius of the Swan Hills plant, in which the government had a stake until last year.

The province in December laid five charges against Chem-Security and Bovar in connection with the toxin discovery and later ordered the company to devise a comprehensive list of toxic chemical sources from the plant.

"While there are already extensive monitoring requirements in the company's existing approval, my department has required the company to do more comprehensive monitoring," Ty Lund, Alberta's minister of environmental protection, said in a statement.

Meanwhile Alberta's provincial health officer John Waters said on Thursday it downgraded a public health advisory issued in December, which recommended wild game taken from within the region not be eaten.
Waters said, however, the people should still limit the amount of meat from the area that they eat. ((Reuters Calgary Bureau (403) 531-1624))
